Part 1 Getting started · Chapter 1

What Roast is, and what it is not

Roast is a free app for people who grow, process, roast, brew or taste coffee. This chapter tells you what it does, what it does not do, and how its parts fit together, before you tap anything.

What Roast is for

Roast keeps the records of a coffee from the plant to the cup. A grower writes down each day's picking. A processor writes down each step from cherry to green coffee. A roaster writes down each roast, and a brewer or taster writes down each cup. Because each record points to the one before it, any cup can be followed back to the plot where it grew.

It runs in your phone's web browser. You do not download it from an app store, and you do not need an account to start.

The path a coffee takes in the app

Every record in Roast sits somewhere on this path. You do not have to use all of it. A home brewer may only ever use the last two steps; a grower who sells cherry may only use the first two.

  1. Plot
  2. Harvest
  3. Process run
  4. Green lot
  5. Roast
  6. Cup

Each arrow is a link the app keeps for you. When you make a green lot from a process run, the green lot knows its run, the run knows its harvests, and the harvests know their plots. You never type the same thing twice.

Why it matters

A buyer, a café or a visitor may ask where a coffee came from and how it was made. If each step points to the one before, the answer is already there. Nobody has to dig through notebooks.

What you get

These promises are written on the Home page under What to expect. They are what the app actually does today.

  1. Free. No ads and nothing to buy.

  2. Your records stay on your phone unless you choose to keep them in an account as well. Chapter 2 explains the choice.

  3. You can take everything out. Lists export as CSV (for Excel or Google Sheets) or JSON. Roasts also export to Artisan and Cropster files. Plots export as the EU plot file (GeoJSON) and to Google Earth.

  4. Every tip names its source: a study, the Coffee Board, or common practice.

  5. It works with no signal. What you enter is kept on the phone and nothing is lost when the network drops.

  6. The app and its code belong to KoffyKraft; your records belong to you.

What Roast is not

Watch out

Roast is not a certificate. It can check each plot against EU forest maps of 2020 and tree loss since then, and it can gather what a European buyer asks for. That is guidance to help you get ready for the EU deforestation rule (EUDR). It does not certify anything, and it does not replace a lawyer, an auditor or the buyer's own checks.

  • Not a guarantee. Advice in the app is a guide. A drying time or a fermentation range is what a named source found, not a promise about your coffee.
  • Not a shop or a marketplace. Nothing is sold through it and nobody pays to use it.
  • Not a judge of people. Records show who entered something, so it can be trusted or corrected. Nothing in the app rates or ranks workers.
  • Not a place where mistakes vanish. A saved record is not deleted. If it was wrong, you correct it, and the change is kept beside it. Chapter 8 shows how.

The four groups on Home

Home sorts everything into four groups. You will meet each of them in this manual.

GroupWhat lives thereChapters
FarmPlots, the map, field log, weather, trails, rows and plants, crop care4 to 7
LotsHarvests, process runs, green lots, passports, the EUDR guide8 to 12
Roast and cupThe Roast timer, Roastbook, graph, colour, brew log, cupping, brew guide, water13 to 17
BusinessTeam and wages, field jobs, sales and money, land and dues, names lists18 to 21
Tip

You do not need to read the whole manual. Read Part 1, then jump to the chapter for the work you do.

Part 1 Getting started · Chapter 2

Putting it on your phone

How to open Roast, keep it on your home screen like any other app, decide whether you want an account, and what happens when there is no signal.

What this part is for

Roast is a web app. It lives at an address, like a website, but once it has opened on your phone it keeps a copy of itself so it opens fast and keeps working without a network. This chapter gets it onto your phone and helps you choose between keeping records only on this phone or also in a private account.

Open it and keep it on your home screen

  1. Open Chrome (Android) or Safari (iPhone) and go to roast.koffykraft.coffee. The first time, Roast opens on Home. You will see the words Coffee, from farm to cup.

  2. Put it on your home screen. On an iPhone: tap the Share button at the bottom of Safari, then Add to Home Screen. On Android: tap the ⋮ menu at the top right of Chrome, then Add to home screen. These menus belong to your phone's browser, not to Roast, so their words can differ a little between phones.

  3. Open Roast from the new icon. It now opens on its own, without the browser's address bar.

Tip

Open it once while you have a signal. That is when the phone keeps its copy of the app. After that it opens even in airplane mode.

With or without an account

You can use everything in Roast without an account. The difference is where your records are kept.

No accountSigned in
Where records liveOnly on this phoneOn this phone and in your private account
Another phone sees themNoYes, once you sign in there with the same email
If the phone is lost or resetGone, unless you saved a backup fileStill in your account
What it costsNothingNothing

Keep going without an account

  1. Tap the round person button at the top right, then Account and sign-in.

  2. Under Continue without an account, tap Continue locally. Nothing else is needed.

Sign in with your email

There is no password. Each time you sign in, Roast emails you a 6-digit code.

  1. On the Account page, find Private cloud account. Type your email in the Email box.

  2. Read the privacy notice (the link is in the sentence beside the tick box). It says what is kept, for how long, and what happens to your records if KoffyKraft closes. If you agree, tick the box.

  3. Tap Send sign-in code. You will see 6-digit code sent to and your email, and a new box for the code.

  4. Open your email, find the sign-in email, and type the 6 digits into the 6-digit code box.

  5. Tap Verify & sign in. The page reloads and you are signed in.

When you are signed in and online, records already on this phone go to your account, and records made on your other phones come in.

Watch out

If you tap Send sign-in code without ticking the box, nothing is sent and the page asks you to read and tick the privacy notice first. After a code is sent, the button rests for 30 seconds before it will send another, so wait for the first email before tapping again. Check your spam folder if it has not arrived.

Tip

Staff who enter records for you can sign in on their own phone with the same account email. Each record still shows who entered it.

Working with no signal

Roast is built for hill farms, drying yards and store rooms where the signal comes and goes.

  • Everything you enter is saved on the phone first. On Origin you will see Saved on this device under the page name, and a saved record shows On this phone.
  • Find works with no signal. It searches the records on this phone.
  • The ? still works. With a signal it opens the full guide on koffykraft.coffee. Without one, it opens the guide kept inside the app.
  • New versions arrive by themselves. The App version card on Account has Check for updates if you want to look now.
Watch out

A few things need the internet because they ask a server: signing in, the land check on a plot, and fetching weather. The app tells you plainly when it needs a connection; nothing you typed is lost.

Watch out

If you use Roast without an account, your records live only in this phone's browser. Clearing the browser's data, or removing the app from the phone, removes them too. Save a backup file now and then. When one is due, Now shows a Keep a copy card that takes you there: after 14 days when your records are only on this phone, after 30 when you are signed in. On Account, Backup reminder lets you change this to weekly, after each save, or off.

Why it matters

Records you cannot lose are records you can trust. Working on the phone first means a bad signal never stops a harvest being written down; an account or a backup file means a lost phone never takes a season's records with it.

Part 1 Getting started · Chapter 3

Your first day

A walk around the app before you record anything: Home, the menu and the ?, Make it yours, the Now page and its tiles, and Find.

What this part is for

Ten minutes here saves an hour later. You will learn where things are, tell the app what you do so your own pages come first, and see how to find any record again.

Home

The first time you open Roast it opens on Home. Home is the map of the whole app: every part is one tap away from here.

  1. At the top is the bar you will see on every page.

    From left to right: KoffyKraft (tap it to come back to Home), the language box, the ?, and the round person button. Below them is the menu, which scrolls sideways.

  2. Under the welcome words is the Find box (Find a plot, lot code, soil, labels) and the dark My Now button. More on both below.

  3. First steps helps you start. Tap I grow, I roast or I brew. You will see a short numbered list for that kind of work, with a button for the first step. For a grower it starts with Add your estate.

    Tap Hide when you no longer need it.

  4. Further down, the groups Farm, Lots, Roast and cup and Business hold a button for each part of the app.

Tip

The language box changes the overviews and explanations into Malayalam, Kannada, Tamil, Spanish or Portuguese. Buttons, field names and numbers stay in English, so this manual still matches what you see.

The ? and the person button

  • The ? opens the guide at the part about the page you are on. With a signal it opens the full guide on koffykraft.coffee; without one, the guide kept inside the app.
  • The person button opens Me: your activity on this phone, and links to Account and sign-in, Shared spaces and My data.

Make it yours

Make it yours asks what you do, so the pages you use most come first. Nothing is hidden: everything else stays one tap away.

  1. Open it from Home (the Make it yours button near the bottom), from the card on Now, or later from Account, where it shows your answers and a Change link.

  2. What do you do? Tick every one that fits: Grow, Process, Roast, Brew, Taste, Buy or sell, Teach or learn.

  3. How deep? Pick Casual, Keen or Professional.

  4. Who uses it? Pick Just me, A few of us or A business. If more than one person uses it, Team joins your pages.

  5. Open the app on: choose the page Roast should open on from now on. Now is the usual choice; a roaster may prefer the Roast timer, a brewer the Brew log.

  6. Tap Show my pages. You land on Now.

You will see the menu change on every page. It now starts with Now, then your own pages (up to seven), then All and Account. Before you answer, the menu stays as it was, so nothing moves without you asking.

Watch out

In this version, your answer to How deep? is kept with your choices but does not yet change which fields the pages show. Every page still shows all of its fields; leave the ones you do not need empty.

Now

Now is the page for today. It shows what is live on this phone: plots to look at, harvests this week, runs in process, green stock and roasts resting.

  1. The tiles across the top count what is live. Tap a tile to jump to its section further down.

  2. Tap the dashed Tiles tile to choose which tiles Now shows. They are grouped from land to cup. Use my activities ticks the ones that match your answers in Make it yours.

  3. Each section has its own quick button on the right, such as + New harvest, + New run, + Add green and + Start roast.

  4. My pages lists your pinned pages. Tap Edit to change them.

  5. Done shelf keeps finished work by coffee season (October to September) and month, so Now stays short.

  6. The bar at the bottom stays in reach of your thumb: New opens a menu to add a harvest, process run, reading, green lot, roast, brew or cup, colour reading or plot. Find opens Find. Home goes to Home. Scan reads a KoffyKraft QR code with the camera, or from a saved photo or screenshot.

Tip

Tap the small i beside the word Now for a reminder of how long things stay live: a run until a green lot is made from it (or 60 days pass), a roast for 30 days while it rests.

Tip

If you only brew or taste, and do not grow, process or roast, the bottom bar changes to brewing actions: New brew, Repeat last and Brew timer.

Find

Find looks through your records, the app's sections and its pages at once.

  1. Type in the Find box on Home or Now, or tap Find on the bottom bar.

  2. Type part of a name or code. A plot name, a lot code like G261024-1, or a word like soil. You will see Your records first, each with its kind on the right (Plot, Green lot and so on).

  3. Tap a result to open it.

You will see Searched on this phone. Works with no signal. under the results.

Why it matters

Codes and names are how records find each other. When you can find a lot by typing three letters, you can answer a buyer's question standing in the store room.

Part 3 From harvest to green coffee · Chapter 8

Logging a harvest

One record for each day's picking: which plots, how many kilos, how ripe, and how sweet. This is the first link between a plot and the coffee that leaves it.

What this part is for

A harvest record says what was picked, where and when. Later, a process run takes its cherry from one or more harvests, and the green lot it makes points back through them to the plots. If the harvest is written down, every bag that follows can be traced.

You need at least one plot before you start (chapter 4). If you have not added one yet, you can still save a harvest and tick its plots later.

Steps

  1. Open Origin from the menu, then the Harvest tab. You will see a line with the season so far (how many harvests, the kilos of cherry, the average Brix) and your harvests, newest first.

  2. Tap + Harvest. You will see New harvest with the Harvest code and Date already filled in. The code is made from the date: H, then year, month and day, then a number for that day (H261102-1 is the first harvest on 2 November 2026).

    Try it in the app ›

  3. If you picked on another day, change the Date. Start time and End time are optional.

  4. Under Plots picked, tick each plot the cherry came from. Then choose the Picking: Selective, Strip, Gleaning or Mixed, and type how many Pickers.

  5. Under Weights, tap + Add basket once for each basket, picker or batch. In each row, put a name in the left box and the kilos in the right box (the one marked kg). You will see the total add up as you type: 3 · total 56 kg beside the button, and Total cherry 56 kg from 3 baskets below.

  6. Under Cherry quality, fill what you know: Ripe %, Under-ripe %, Over-ripe % and Floaters %. For sweetness, tap + Add Brix reading once for each refractometer reading. You will see Average Brix with the number of readings and their range.

  7. Add the Weather and any Notes if you like. Under People and hours, + Person adds the people who worked. Under Photos, Take a photo or From gallery.

  8. Tap Save at the bottom. You will see Saved for a moment, and the new harvest at the top of the list with its kilos, picking, ripeness and Brix.

Watch out

A weight in the name box. The basket row has two boxes. If the kilos go into the left box, the app reads them as the basket's name: the total does not grow and no Total cherry line appears. Look for the total after every row. If it is missing, move the number into the box marked kg.

Tip

You do not have to weigh every basket. One row called Day total with the day's kilos works just as well. Use separate rows when you want to see who picked what, or to pay by weight.

Tip

Not sure what counts as ripe, or when to pick? The Crop care, harvest link under the weights opens the app's own guide to what to pick, when and how, with its sources named.

Fixing a mistake

Records in Roast are not deleted. When something was wrong, you correct it, and the app keeps the change beside the record.

  1. Tap the harvest in the list to open it.

  2. Change the number or the words, and tap Save.

  3. At the bottom of the record, tap Entered by… to see who entered it and every change since: the date and time, who made it, the field and its old and new value.

If a whole harvest should not be there (entered twice, say), open it and tap Void at the bottom. The app asks for a reason. A voided harvest leaves the lists but is kept, and you can restore it from Voided at the end of the list. Anything already linked to it keeps its link.

Why it matters

A buyer who trusts your records needs to know they were not quietly changed. Keeping the change beside the record, with who and when, is what makes a record worth trusting.

What comes next

The cherry goes to processing. Chapter 9 shows how a process run takes this harvest as its source, so its kilos and its plots carry forward on their own.

Part 3 From harvest to green coffee · Chapter 9

Process runs

Everything that happens between cherry and green coffee: floating, pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, resting and hulling. One run, step by step, with times, weights and readings.

What this part is for

A process run follows one batch of cherry through its steps. Each step keeps its own start and end time, the kilos in and out, and any readings you take (temperature, pH, Brix and others). The run takes its cherry from your harvests, so it already knows the plots, and the green lot you make at the end takes its weight from the run.

Start a run

  1. Open Origin, then the Process tab, and tap + Process. You will see New processing run with a Process code made from today's date (P, then year, month and day).

    Try it in the app ›

  2. Choose the Pathway: Washed, Natural, one of the honeys, anaerobic, or one of the fermentation-led processes further down the list. The pathway is required.

  3. Under Source harvests, tick the harvests that went into this batch. Each shows its code, date and kilos. You will see Cherry in add up from the harvests you ticked.

    If the cherry was not logged as a harvest (bought cherry, say), leave the harvests unticked and type the kilos in Cherry in (if not from harvests) instead.

  4. Check Started, the day the run began.

Add the steps

You can add steps one at a time as the work happens, or start from a ready-made list and fill it in as you go.

  1. Under Steps, open Start from a ready-made protocol (optional) and pick one, such as Washed arabica, Indian estate (Coffee Board of India). Each protocol names its source. You will see 7 steps added. Fill in times and weights as you go. and the steps in order. Each step already carries a short guide from the source: how long it usually takes and what to watch for.

    To build your own list instead, choose a step type in the box under the steps and tap + Add step. Use ↑ to move a step up and × to remove it.

Work through each step

  1. When a step begins, tap Start now. You will see the step turn to Running with a clock that keeps counting. When the step is over, tap End now. If you ended it by mistake, Still running opens it again.

  2. Type the kilos in In kg and Out kg, and any other boxes the step has (floaters, water, the vessel or bed, notes).

  3. Readings. Under Measurements, tap the measures you want for this step to switch them on: Temp °C, pH, °Brix, Air °C, Air RH %, and others depending on the step. Each one you switch on shows a guide range underneath; tap Guide values and sources after the last step to see where each range comes from. Tap + Reading now each time you measure. A new row appears with the time already filled; type the numbers.

    Once a measure has two or more readings, a small chart appears above the rows, with the guide range shaded.

  4. Photos as you go. Each step has its own Photo button for pictures of the tank, the bed or the parchment.

Watch out

Save after each visit. Start now, End now and new readings are kept only when you tap Save. If you leave the page or close the app before saving, they are gone and the step shows Not started again. Make it a habit: start the step, type the reading, tap Save.

Tip

You can add a reading from anywhere: on Now, tap New, then Reading (pH, Brix, temp, photo), and pick the live run.

Fermenting with a yeast or starter

  1. In a Fermentation step, choose a method that uses a yeast or starter, such as With yeast / starter. You will see an Inoculation box. Pick the Product and type the Grams used. Rehydration water, its temperature and minutes, the price per kg and the time it was added to the tank are there too. You will see the product's own notes, a suggested dose for the kilos in this step, and how to rehydrate it. The figures come from the maker's published sheets.

Save

  1. Tap Save whenever you like; you do not have to wait for the run to finish. Come back to it from the Process tab and carry on. You will see the run's own page: the chain from plot to harvest to this run, and buttons for Share to a space, Image or PDF and Passport and QR.

Watch out

Out more than in. If a step's Out kg is bigger than its In kg, or the first step takes more kilos than its harvests weighed, the run still saves, and the app tells you what to check (for example Pulping: out 90 kg is more than in 85 kg). It never changes your numbers by itself. Usually a number went into the wrong box.

Watch out

The end before the start. If you type an end time earlier than the start, the step says so in red. Fix the end time, or tap Still running.

Why it matters

Cup quality is often made or lost in processing. When every run keeps its times, kilos and readings, you can compare this season's best lot with last season's and see what you did differently. Outturn (green out as a share of cherry in) is worked out for you once the green weight is known.

What comes next

When the coffee is dry, rested and hulled, it becomes a green lot. Chapter 10 shows how the green lot takes its weight from this run.

Part 3 From harvest to green coffee · Chapter 10

Green lots

The green coffee itself: how much there is, what it cost, how dry it is, where it is stored, and what is left as roasts and sales draw on it. Your own coffee or coffee you bought in.

What this part is for

A green lot is what goes to the roaster. For your own coffee, it points back to its process run, and through the run to the harvests and plots. For bought coffee, it keeps the origin as the seller states it. Every roast you make later picks a green lot as its source, and the lot's stock goes down by itself.

Make a green lot from your own run

  1. Open Origin, then the Green tab, and tap + Green lot. You will see New green lot with a Green lot code made from today's date (G, then year, month and day).

    Try it in the app ›

  2. Give it a Name people will recognise, such as Upper block natural robusta.

  3. Under From process, pick the run it came from. You will see the chain from that run, and a message: Green weight filled from the run, with the kilos. The weight is taken from the run's last Out kg. Change it if the scale says otherwise.

  4. Under This lot, check the Green weight (required). Type the Cost of this lot if you know it: what you paid, or what it cost to grow and process. You will see the cost per green kilo, and about what a roasted kilo costs at 15% weight loss. Each roast later shows its own. Add the Bags and the Bag size if it is bagged.

  5. Under Quality, type the Moisture % from your meter. If you have no water activity meter, the app gives an estimate from the moisture (between 10 and 13% only), and says whether it is good for storage. The estimate is worked out from arabica figures, so treat it as rough, more so for robusta. Add Density g/L, Screen size, Grade and Cup score when you have them, and where it is kept under Storage.

  6. Tap Save. You will see the lot's own page: its name, the chain back to plot, harvest and run, how much is left, and buttons for each part of the lot: This lot, Quality and stock, EUDR, Sack labels and For a buyer.

Coffee you bought in

Leave From process empty and fill Bought coffee: origin as the seller states it: Farm or washing station, Producer, Region, Country, Variety, Process, Altitude, m, Harvest, Bought from, Lot or auction number and Invoice date. Type exactly what the seller's papers say. Then carry on from step 4.

Watch out

A green lot with no process and nothing under Bought from still saves, but the app tells you: Not linked to a process. Pick its process, or fill Bought from to mark it bought in. Without one of the two, nobody can tell where the coffee came from.

Watch out

If the green weight is more than the run gave out, the app says so when you save (Green weight … kg is more than the process gave out). It keeps the number you typed. Check the scale, or check the run's last step.

Keep the stock right

The stock goes down as roasts use the lot. For everything else (a sample sent, a bag sold, a recount in the store), add a line.

  1. On the lot's page, tap Quality and stock. You will see how many kilos are left of the lot, how many full bags that makes, and where it is stored.

  2. Tap the line you need: + Moisture for a new moisture reading (the lot keeps every reading, so you can watch it dry out or take up water in storage). + Count/move after counting the bags or moving them. + Adjust for anything else that changes the kilos.

  3. Fill in the line and tap Add line, then Save at the bottom.

Watch out

New stock lines are kept only when you tap Save at the bottom of the lot. The page reminds you: New lines are kept when you tap Save.

Sack labels

  1. On the lot's page, tap Sack labels. You will see one label for each bag, 100 by 50 mm, with a QR code, the lot code, its name and estate, the process, moisture and date, and Bag 1 of 1.

  2. Tap the Print button at the top. Each label prints on its own page.

The QR opens this lot in the app. Once the lot has a passport (chapter 11), the QR opens the passport instead, which anyone can check.

Tip

If the labels do not open, your phone may be blocking pop-ups for the app. Allow them, then tap Sack labels again.

Why it matters

Moisture and water activity decide how long green coffee keeps. The app's own guide (from the ICO, the SCA and a long Cafe Imports study) aims for 11 to 11.5% moisture for long storage: above about 11.7%, water activity usually passes 0.61, and lots above 0.61 lost more cup score in transit. A reading on the lot every few weeks shows a drift while there is still time to act.

What comes next

Chapter 11 turns this green lot into a lot passport with a QR any buyer can check. Chapter 12 covers the EUDR section of the lot, for coffee that will be sold into Europe. Roasts that use this lot are in chapter 13.
